江流浩蕩-伊瓜蘇瀑布.descriptionEn: Vast waters move between heaven and earth, circling back again and again, nurturing all living things. Ink surges, a universe beneath the brush; coming or going without intent, the spirit wanders beyond the world. Painted by Zhijing in the year Bingwu: the great Iguazu Falls.
江流浩蕩-伊瓜蘇瀑布.curatorNoteEn: A monumental work capturing the grandeur of Iguazu Falls, the brush steady and the energy unbroken. The falls thunder forward layer upon layer — the majesty of nature, and also the steady growth of character. Within movement there is virtue; within force there is the Way. As heaven moves without rest, strength forms the bones; as water nourishes in silence, generosity fills the heart. Standing before it, one is moved not only by its power but by the inner cultivation and breadth of spirit it carries.

千峯曙色-玉山日初雲海.titleEn: Dawn over a Thousand Peaks – Sunrise and Sea of Clouds at Yushan
千峯曙色-玉山日初雲海.descriptionEn: Clouds rise for a hundred miles beyond heaven and earth; dawn on a thousand peaks reflects the true nature of things. With a clear heart one contemplates the Way, and emptiness gives birth to light; in one moment of clarity, all things unfold.
千峯曙色-玉山日初雲海.curatorNoteEn: This painting portrays the towering majesty of Yushan (Jade Mountain), with mist as its breath and the light of dawn as its spirit. The mountain is massive yet never heavy; among the layered ridges, empty space becomes drifting cloud, giving heaven and earth their own rhythm of breathing. Its beauty lies in stillness within motion: the flowing clouds speak of passing time, the unmoving summit of steadfast resolve. Above all, a single line of morning light breaks through the mist, illuminating both the land and the human heart — a sign of renewal and of the will to keep striving.

霜林涵秀.descriptionEn: The frosted woods hold autumn's beauty; falling leaves sound like a zither. All things should rest on nothing; the voice of autumn enters my heart.
霜林涵秀.curatorNoteEn: An autumn forest dressed in red leaves, the ground covered with fallen ones — poem after poem of autumn, alive with spirit. Light mist drifts through the trees, creating deep, hazy layers, while a path of fallen leaves leads the eye into the heart of the painting. Two figures walk slowly along it, turning a natural scene into a human one — as if "walking on, we walked into time," or as if "falling leaves are not leaving, but another way of standing still." There is painting in the poem, and poetry in the painting.

玉山雲瀑.descriptionEn: Jade ridges soar into the heavens; flying clouds descend from the far sky. Stillness holds a myriad movements; pure air is one with heaven.
玉山雲瀑.curatorNoteEn: The majestic main peak of Yushan stands between heaven and earth, while below it a waterfall of cloud pours past the mountain's foot. In the play of stillness and motion — "the mountain comes alive through the clouds, the clouds rise and fall with the mountain" — heaven and earth merge in quiet ease. The painting depicts not only form but force and spirit: the mountain is the body, the cloud its movement; stillness and motion complete each other in endless renewal.

火炎雄渾-火炎山.descriptionEn: The mighty Fire Mountain is nature's own creation; a thousand cliffs and ten thousand ravines enter my heart. Heaven and earth become one color, emptiness gives birth to light; light clouds and gentle wind, the same now as in ancient times.
火炎雄渾-火炎山.curatorNoteEn: Through alternating dense and pale ink and soft washes, this painting captures the steep, dramatic presence of Huoyan (Fire) Mountain in Sanyi. Towering cliffs, as if cut by axe and blade, rise out of deep mist; ink and ochre blend across layered rock faces to reveal the mountain's rugged texture and the marks of time. Clouds drift through the peaks, giving movement to the hard bones of the mountain, while a few pale winter trees add a note of solitude and grace. Expansive in spirit yet restrained in brushwork, it is a landscape of the mind between loftiness and quiet emptiness.

排雲赤壁-火炎山.titleEn: Red Cliffs Parting the Clouds – Huoyan Mountain
排雲赤壁-火炎山.descriptionEn: Red cliffs rise through the clouds into the sky; vast misty waters hold the whole world. Ink paints wondrous peaks into a scroll; a line of white egrets flies into the blue.
排雲赤壁-火炎山.curatorNoteEn: This large work of Huoyan Mountain in Sanyi shows the steep, boundless character of Taiwan's mountain landscape. The main peak soars upward, its layered cliffs sharp as if carved. Painted mainly in pure ink with light touches of ochre, the rock glows with the last warmth of the setting sun. Distant hills fade into mist, white clouds rise and fall among the ridges, and the rugged valleys breathe with quiet. A line of white egrets flies off into the sky — the living, spiritual highlight of the whole painting.

別有洞天-九曲洞.titleEn: A Hidden World – Tunnel of Nine Turns
別有洞天-九曲洞.descriptionEn: Ink paints a thousand layers of cliff; light gives rise to countless threads of mist. Mountains and rivers are my teachers; the Nine Turns stir the heart.
別有洞天-九曲洞.curatorNoteEn: Painted from life at the Tunnel of Nine Turns in Taroko Gorge. Bold brushstrokes build up the texture and hardness of the rock layer by layer, while carefully reserved white space within the cliff forms the caves. Light is painted with heavy ink: brilliant rays pierce the darkness and illuminate the winding gorge, bringing the whole painting to life. A few small visitors admire the scenery, leading the viewer toward the light and marking the focal point of the work.

雲捲秋光-清秋.titleEn: Clouds Rolling in Autumn Light – Clear Autumn
雲捲秋光-清秋.descriptionEn: Clouds roll in as a thousand peaks gather; wind races and ten thousand valleys open. Autumn light floats on distant water; all things linger at ease. Far waters faint in the evening mist, silent peaks enter autumn. White clouds ask nothing of the human world; a free, pure breeze falls before the painting.
雲捲秋光-清秋.curatorNoteEn: Tall mountains rise in the distance, peaks wrapped in drifting mist. Following the painting downward, distant water and floating clouds flow on and on — a clear, light autumn scene where the far water shares one color with the sky and autumn trees sway in the wind. Mist moves through the whole composition. Using only light yellow-green and ink with ochre, the painting is harmonious, elegant and full of life, leaving a sense of being beyond the dust of the world — an expression of the artist's inner spaciousness, deep calm and ease, and her lifelong search for the great beauty of heaven and earth.

煙波物外-秋聲.titleEn: Misty Waters Beyond the World – The Sound of Autumn
煙波物外-秋聲.descriptionEn: Vast misty waters enter my painting; beyond the world I come and go freely all my life. The sound of autumn and I once made a promise: to meet among the white clouds every year. A distant waterfall opens autumn's colors; cold clouds enter the green hills. A stream flows without end; in stillness one glimpses heaven's secret.
煙波物外-秋聲.curatorNoteEn: A mountain home in late autumn. Distant peaks rise layer upon layer, wrapped in cloud, and a waterfall pours from on high as the source of all things. Gold and russet weave through the forest, rich with autumn; a stream winds toward the viewer, murmuring as it flows. In a corner of the woods a home sits hidden and peaceful, at one with heaven and earth. The whole is both grand and secluded — the abundance of nature and the quiet joy of a hermit's life.

櫻紅雲瀑-山上人家.titleEn: Cherry Blossoms and Cloud Falls – Home on the Mountain
櫻紅雲瀑-山上人家.descriptionEn: Red cherry blossoms reach the distant hills; cloud falls pour down the empty mountains. Amid ten thousand acres of mist, I come and go without intent.
櫻紅雲瀑-山上人家.curatorNoteEn: Painted at "Home on the Mountain" in Wufeng, Hsinchu, famed for its dreamlike avenues of pink cherry blossoms and spectacular seas of cloud. Among rolling hills the cherry trees bloom in light and deep tones, like dawn clouds or mist; a waterfall of cloud surges in from afar, gathering and dispersing, while mountain homes appear and disappear within it. Pale ink sets an airy mood and rich color brings the sea of blossoms to life — a peaceful paradise far from the noise of the world. Where is the best place on earth? Half the mountain in mist, half the mountain at ease.

松下聽泉.titleEn: Listening to the Spring Beneath the Pines
松下聽泉.descriptionEn: Deep in the clouds, no one knows who has entered the mountain; beneath the pines, listening to the spring, I forget the dust of the world. Twin waterfalls fly beyond a thousand peaks; a clear, quiet heart faces the boundless.
松下聽泉.curatorNoteEn: A restrained, elegant ink painting that rewards long looking. Dark pines, twin waterfalls leaping into the air, and a lone figure seated beneath a pine, gazing at the falls. Two birds soar freely among the cliffs, and terraced fields and homes appear faintly in the distance — the ideal landscape one can live in and wander through. The painting conveys a mind detached from worldly cares and returned to nature, in the spirit of the poem: "Somewhere on this mountain, but the clouds are too deep to know where."

杏雪吹雲.descriptionEn: Apricot blossoms like snow blow into white clouds; the green grass is fresh and new. Leisurely and content, in simplicity one finds what is true.
杏雪吹雲.curatorNoteEn: Fresh, gentle and far-reaching: apricot blossoms like snow spread out into clouds, and a band of green meadow stretches across the painting, letting it breathe between solid and empty. White sheep graze unhurried upon it — stillness in motion, motion in stillness. It calms the heart: leisurely, content, and true in its simplicity.

遠水秋山.descriptionEn: Autumn mountains after fresh rain; distant waters glow with clear, quiet light. When the restless mind comes to rest, one enters the working of nature without effort.
遠水秋山.curatorNoteEn: A broad, warm golden-autumn scene. Distant mountains in pale ink form the framework, with mist pushing the space further and further back. In the middle ground, ochre-gold and mineral green weave through the trees like light entering the forest. Near the water the brushwork turns fluid and the ink moist, contrasting with the stillness of the woods. A bridge and traces of people give the landscape human warmth. Solid and empty, warm and cool answer one another — the ripeness of autumn and the endless renewal of life, in the spirit of "learn from nature outside, find its source within."

萬年峽谷.descriptionEn: A thread of misty sound falls on the green peaks; the ancient canyon plays a clear melody. Mountains and rivers know heaven and earth without a word; flowing water, without intent, has seen past and present.
萬年峽谷.curatorNoteEn: The grandeur of Wannian (Ten-Thousand-Year) Canyon. A distant waterfall plunges from high cliffs through the mist, and the stream winds through countless layers of rock, carved over tens of thousands of years into ancient, extraordinary forms. Built-up ink, textured strokes and washes render the weight of the stone, with misty clouds lending an air of vastness — nature's astonishing craftsmanship, and the endless turning of heaven and earth. Standing before it is like entering a primeval valley: awe-struck, one feels the quiet beauty of a river that has flowed for ages.

千峰瑞雪.titleEn: Auspicious Snow on a Thousand Peaks
千峰瑞雪.descriptionEn: A thousand peaks hold auspicious snow; ten thousand valleys are wrapped in spring mist. Sitting and gazing at the vast cloudy mountains, the heart grows as wide as heaven and earth.
千峰瑞雪.curatorNoteEn: Northern mountains: snow still lingers on the far peaks and clouds drift lightly by. In the middle ground spring begins to appear, a mountain path winds, and waterfalls run hidden between the slopes. By the water nearby a village sits with boats at rest, motion and stillness in balance. Painted mainly in ink with light color, the brushwork is both strong and moist, carrying the grandeur of mountains and the warmth of human life. Moving from cold to warmth, from far to near, it expresses the Eastern ideal of a landscape one can wander in, live in, and contemplate.

雲行無盡-風有自己的方向.titleEn: Endless Drifting Clouds – The Wind Has Its Own Direction
雲行無盡-風有自己的方向.descriptionEn: Mist floats over ten thousand valleys as clouds move beneath the brush; a thousand forests of layered ink — mountains held within the heart.
雲行無盡-風有自己的方向.curatorNoteEn: With ink alone, the spirit of clouds moving in the wind comes vividly to life. Ink becomes mist, a few inches hold a thousand miles, and the brush writes the heart's depths with free and easy grace — a beauty unique to this painting. Its special quality is how a single tone of ink conveys vast heaven and earth and the clear air of the mountains with such movement. Who could breathe clouds onto paper without mountains already in their heart?

此心安處.titleEn: Where the Heart Is at Peace
此心安處.descriptionEn: A thousand great halls hold all things; wherever the heart is at peace is my home.
此心安處.curatorNoteEn: An ink painting of many houses, receding from near to far in flowing ink and drifting mist. It draws on Du Fu's wish for "ten thousand great halls to shelter all the poor scholars of the world, unshaken by wind and rain, steady as a mountain," and on Su Shi, who remained serene through hardship: "Wherever the heart is at peace is my home." Through the flowing ink and open space of contemporary ink painting, these ideas become a state of mind one can dwell in and contemplate.

水域・帆影・去留之間.titleEn: Water, Sails, Between Leaving and Staying
水域・帆影・去留之間.descriptionEn: Distant waters hold empty white; masts and sails enter the boundless haze. What do they resemble as they drift? Going or staying, the shadow follows the form.
水域・帆影・去留之間.curatorNoteEn: Reserved white space suggests a faint expanse of water and drifting sails, between dream and reality. Vertical lines — like masts, like rain, like slices of time — divide the space and connect it again; horizontal boats, their reflections, floating islets and a dreamlike far shore mirror one another, so that time (vertical) and space (horizontal) meet. Solid and empty arise together; motion and stillness become one. Between leaving and staying, the wind knows the way. Boats come and go while their reflections remain — an instant made eternal.

眾妙之門.descriptionEn: All mysteries float on the calm water, drifting lightly into sea and sky. The mysterious gate knows no coming or going; all things give rise to mist of their own. Half a wall of haze enters the great mystery; faint light like water crosses the cold mist. A lone boat does not head for the human world; it sits and watches emptiness give birth to ten thousand streams.
眾妙之門.curatorNoteEn: The top of the painting is framed like a doorway — as the Tao Te Ching says, "Mystery upon mystery, the gate to all wonders." Large areas of white are left open; within this ethereal void, light and mist flow in and meet the lively water below in overlapping strokes, fluid and understated. Through vapor, light and the rhythm of ink, the painting builds a space between being and non-being. A boat, barely there, moves from the solid into the empty, from scene into state of mind — something felt rather than said. It is a spiritual space at the border of form and emptiness, close to what Laozi called the Tao.

靜泊.descriptionEn: Fishing boats moor by the misty shore; at daybreak they will head out to sea.
靜泊.curatorNoteEn: In ink of varied depth and moisture, a harbor at the edge of dawn: a faint brightening along the horizon, boats moored in the water, a few people aboard waiting for the call to set sail toward the rising sun and the open sea — the start of another good day. Heaven and earth are just waking. Mooring is a time of quiet gathering, waiting for the moment day breaks to sail toward the light.

甦醒.descriptionEn: Empty white rises along the shore; the boats wait for the dawn wind.
甦醒.curatorNoteEn: A faint glow of sky over a quiet village. Fishing boats rest along the shore among a forest of masts, and one boat readies itself to set out before sunrise, a few birds keeping it company. The stillness is full of life. In misty ink, light and shadow are rendered with great delicacy — the warmth of dawn over a river village and the deep feeling of passing years — as if reminding us to follow nature's setting moon and rising sun: "As heaven moves ever onward, so the noble person strives without ceasing."

啟航.descriptionEn: The water's edge holds a faint glow; the boats' shadows slip into silence.
啟航.curatorNoteEn: Part of the harbor series, this painting uses the rhythm of ink to create a misty waterfront at dawn, the sky low and the light soft. Boats and houses stand mirrored in still water, reflection and reality blending like a dream. At the center, a small boat about to depart and several boats already moving form the focal point — delicate and moving. The fishing harbor wakes in the morning light. The boat has not yet sailed far, yet one already feels the distance; the sky is not fully bright, yet hope is already visible — setting out again after the long night, just before dawn.

覺照.descriptionEn: Pale moonlight pierces the clouds, shining on things as they truly are.
覺照.curatorNoteEn: Painted on gold xuan paper with pale ink as breath, the surface seems faintly lit, like an ancient mirror holding the moon. Layers of mist dissolve the mountain between presence and absence, between dream and waking. Soft moonlight spills through the haze, casting a clear light over the land and all things. The simplest of brushwork describes the vastest of realms. Solid and empty merge, form dissolving toward formlessness — echoing "form is emptiness, emptiness is form," and the Daoist sayings that "being and non-being give rise to each other" and "the great image has no form."

山高月小.descriptionEn: The mountain is high, the moon small, the night sky clear (and one longs to climb the blue heavens and embrace the bright moon).
山高月小.curatorNoteEn: A small ink painting on the theme of mountain and moon, unified in a minimal palette. The mountain is built with dry, flying-white strokes and layered ink, the brushwork free yet powerful; mist in pale washes opens the space layer by layer. The moon in the upper right is faint, blending into the atmosphere — present yet almost absent. The high mountain and small moon reveal the vastness of nature and how small we are within it, while the ridges, rising almost to the sky, stir the wish "to climb the blue heavens and embrace the bright moon."

天宇金鏡.descriptionEn: The bright moon rises over the heavenly mountains — alone, in communion with the spirit of heaven and earth.
天宇金鏡.curatorNoteEn: On a dark ground, a golden full moon is left in reserve, hanging high like a golden mirror in the sky. The mountain is woven from silver-white and blue; the strokes look unrestrained but are built up layer by layer into inner depth. The composition is simple — one moon, one peak — creating a lofty spiritual space with the fewest elements. As Zhuangzi said, "alone, in communion with the spirit of heaven and earth": keeping the heart free and independent, in tune with nature, embodying openness, acceptance, and a wisdom in which self and world are forgotten.

與誰同坐.descriptionEn: With whom shall I sit? The bright moon, the clear breeze, and I.
與誰同坐.curatorNoteEn: Layers of blue-black build the weight of earth and mountain, deep and steady. The main peak rises in concentrated strokes, outlining the majesty of Yushan, while a soft-toned moon above sets gentleness against strength. Simple and powerful, it shows the beauty of contemporary ink painting where force and restraint live together. It recalls Su Dongpo's line, "With whom shall I sit? The bright moon, the clear breeze, and I" — a picture of complete solitude and freedom, and of a heart at ease beyond worldly things.

流光-月娘嫁水.titleEn: Flowing Light – The Moon Marries the Water
流光-月娘嫁水.descriptionEn: The Moon Maiden weds the water and follows it to the ends of the earth.
流光-月娘嫁水.curatorNoteEn: Moonlight like water, like a stream, falls from the void into the world like a waterfall — not only the visual focus but a spiritual symbol, like an awakened mind coming from emptiness and flowing through everything without obstruction. Heavy ink forms the body, flowing white the movement; stillness and motion hold each other. The moonlight becomes a person who "marries" the water — a beautiful cosmic romance of sky and water as one, together to the end: moonlight and its reflection, never parting, bound in life and death.

初昇-月華如洗.descriptionEn: Ink dyes the clear glow across the whole sky.
初昇-月華如洗.curatorNoteEn: Ink sets the tone of heaven and earth. A young crescent moon rises faintly at the sky's edge over a quiet, cold pond, where a few white egrets move lightly through the rising mist. In the vastness there is light; in the silence, sound. The moon is not full, yet it accords with Laozi: "Great perfection seems incomplete." The egrets at the water's edge bring life to the stillness — a realm where small movements are seen within great silence.

相契-水月交融.descriptionEn: The moon gives rise to a transformed realm; the heart becomes its own light.
相契-水月交融.curatorNoteEn: Painted to express a feeling that came from deep within. In a misty night, the moon is just rising; water and moon shine on each other, moonlight melts into the sky, and flowing light like water dissolves into the heart. All is still — luminous, clear, free, with heart and spirit as one. The painting moves from the concrete (the moon) to the abstract (light and breath), going beyond a scene into a state of mind. The moon gives rise to a transformed realm; the heart becomes its own light.

無住-光行太初.titleEn: Unabiding – Light Travels from the Beginning
無住-光行太初.descriptionEn: The moon rises in the void; its light travels without abiding.
無住-光行太初.curatorNoteEn: The moon glimmers at the edge of the sky like footsteps from time immemorial, quietly watching over the planets of the universe. White planes and lines, like star trails and the Milky Way, carry horizontal motion, while golden lines streak down like meteors — like the speed of light, like a stream of consciousness. Horizontal and vertical, stillness and motion collide, opening a view into a cosmic field: a linear space where many layers exist at once.

天網-萬縷流光.titleEn: Heaven's Net – Ten Thousand Strands of Light
天網-萬縷流光.descriptionEn: Heaven's net — ten thousand strands of flowing light enter the painting.
天網-萬縷流光.curatorNoteEn: In the vast universe a golden moon slowly rises while white lines cross and interweave like flowing laser light or the speed of light — a lively, highly original image of a "heavenly net." The net describes the light and energy of the cosmos: the starry sky, beams and fields of energy made poetic and almost alive. The invisible energy of the universe and light passing between the stars become a vast, interconnected net of light, full of spirit and life.

光渡-月行寒山.titleEn: Crossing Light – The Moon over Cold Mountains
光渡-月行寒山.descriptionEn: Crossing light — the moon travels through the ages; its light crosses the cold mountains.
光渡-月行寒山.curatorNoteEn: Across the vast sky, icy mountains stand in rows, and a new moon shines unchanged from ancient times to now: "the moon travels through the ages; its light crosses the cold mountains." Lines express light coming from the universe, full of rhythm and boundless tension. The moon is always silent, the ice mountains wordless, heaven and earth vast — yet the light keeps moving forward, "alone, in communion with the spirit of heaven and earth." The artist's wish for the viewer: "in the boundless, keep the light within your heart."

照見-萬頃冰原.titleEn: Seeing Clearly – Endless Fields of Ice
照見-萬頃冰原.descriptionEn: Seeing clearly — endless fields of ice lit in a single moment.
照見-萬頃冰原.curatorNoteEn: Semi-abstract ink combining flying-white, flowing lines and splashed ink. Piercing, icy strokes give the glacier its hardness and cold, weaving a sense of cosmic time and space. A new moon is faintly edged in gold, revealing points of starlight as snow flies over a thousand mountains — as the saying goes, "a room dark for a thousand years is lit by a single lamp." True light is never dazzling; it keeps a little tenderness within ages of quiet stillness, and lights the world.

回望-由月球回望地球.titleEn: Looking Back – Earth Seen from the Moon
回望-由月球回望地球.descriptionEn: Looking back — a glance full of light and lingering tenderness.
回望-由月球回望地球.curatorNoteEn: Seen from the surface of the moon looking toward Earth, the composition differs from her other works. The foreground is silent, desolate and cold, almost soundless, while the blue-green Earth in the distance floats in the sky like a living, breathing being. The lunar surface below is rendered simply with reserved white, making the universe feel even vaster. Earth and moon travel along their orbits in delicate balance, looking back at each other tenderly — moving us with the mysterious power present everywhere in the cosmos.

太初-心月照無涯.titleEn: The Beginning – The Moon of the Heart Shines Without End
太初-心月照無涯.descriptionEn: The beginning — the moon of the heart shines without end.
太初-心月照無涯.curatorNoteEn: Crimson clouds fill the sky and moonlight streams down. Layers of red and black create the unity of heaven and earth, and golden brush marks reflect shimmering light on the water. The moon hangs high over vast misty waves; solid and empty, motion and stillness answer one another. The painting carries both the vastness of the cosmos and the clarity of the heart's source — like standing at the moment before heaven and earth separated, or the moment of first awakening: light found in silence, the self found in the boundless.

照水紅蕖.descriptionEn: Red lotus mirrored in water, its fragrance faint and fine.
照水紅蕖.curatorNoteEn: A hazy moon above, deep still water below, and red lotus blooming just where water meets sky — a strikingly contemporary scene where solid and empty, motion and stillness reflect one another. The mood is restrained yet full of life. The light does not shine from outside but rises from mist and empty space, close to what Chan Buddhism calls "the light of one's own nature." The lotus is not bound to likeness; still waters run deep, answering the distant moon. In a dreamlike haze, it expresses a bond that is near yet far, never letting go.

心燈-燭荷.titleEn: Lamp of the Heart – Candle Lotus
心燈-燭荷.descriptionEn: In lighting the way for others, we also light our own.
心燈-燭荷.curatorNoteEn: In a pond simplified to its essence, a few lotus buds are placed like candles that light up the painting. Against the deep background a faint skylight shows through, a thoughtful touch that brings the whole work to life. There is no moon and no sun, yet there is light — light that comes not from the sky but from awareness within. The highest light goes beyond physical illumination; it is a projection of the spirit, where the Eastern "image of the mind" meets Western light and shadow. Its message: in lighting the way for others, we also light our own.

得意忘象.titleEn: Grasping the Meaning, Forgetting the Image
得意忘象.curatorNoteEn: Moving between the figurative and the abstract, faint lotus shapes and soft light create a spiritual field "between likeness and unlikeness." Between ink painting and contemporary art, with a minimal palette, calligraphic lines and layers of soaking ink, it builds a "space of the spirit" between landscape and inner image. The work keeps the Eastern ink spirit of living rhythm and of depicting the real through the empty, while carrying the emotional field and sense of space of Western modern abstraction.

流霞-動靜不二.titleEn: Flowing Clouds of Dusk – Motion and Stillness Are One
流霞-動靜不二.descriptionEn: Red willows mirror the flowing sunset clouds; white plumes drift into the evening mist. The wind comes, with no going or staying; in motion and in stillness, all is at peace.
流霞-動靜不二.curatorNoteEn: A work of striking presence. Above, a broad expanse of russet red, like glowing evening clouds lighting willows in the wind, its bold vertical strokes moving freely and carrying a sense of time and moving air. Below, egrets gather — some flying, some standing — orderly in their movement, answering the force above with breath and spirit. Movement above and response below, solid and empty, create a natural balance between motion and stillness, weight and lightness. More than a landscape, it is an inner state: motion and stillness are one — "walking is Zen, sitting is Zen; in speech or silence, movement or rest, the body is at peace."

虛實 - 合抱之木.titleEn: Empty and Solid – The Great Tree
虛實 - 合抱之木.descriptionEn: A tree that fills one's arms grows from a tiny shoot; a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
虛實 - 合抱之木.curatorNoteEn: Built on a split composition, the painting is divided into two realms. On the left, a pine in traditional ink brushwork, vigorous and natural; on the right, an abstract trunk in heavy gold and texture, full of contemporary tension. A vertical line between them is both a gap and a passage, letting the two sides converse and pass into each other — small changes becoming great transformation. As the Tao Te Ching says: "A tree that fills one's arms grows from a tiny shoot; a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step."

光流-有無相生.titleEn: Streams of Light – Being and Non-Being Give Rise to Each Other
光流-有無相生.descriptionEn: Streams of light — being and non-being give rise to each other; a rainbow spans the blue sky.
光流-有無相生.curatorNoteEn: Deep blue, built up layer by layer, creates an almost infinite depth. Golden vertical strokes rise above like pillars of light, flames or a city skyline, ascending between solid and empty. The contrast of gold and blue is intense — like the light of civilization in the night, or the fire of awakening in a dark valley. The lower part is calm and deep, the upper full of upward energy: a life journey from stillness to blossoming, from silence to form. Fine red and green lines suggest the rhythm of a city, the rise and fall of the stock market, or the beating of a heart. In abstract language it holds a profound idea, the Daoist contemplation: "All things arise together, and I watch them return."

野百合也有春天.titleEn: Even the Wild Lily Has Its Spring
野百合也有春天.descriptionEn: A single smiling bloom — even the wild lily has its spring.
野百合也有春天.curatorNoteEn: A modern ink painting: an ink ground overlaid with vermilion, with white space on the right as if light were shining through a window onto white lilies, bringing the clear air of the valley into the painting. Gold lines add movement. The lily blooms at ease like a faint light in the night, a symbol that life holds endless hope even in darkness. In a lonely corner of the valley, "even the wild lily has its spring" — everyone deserves love and happiness.

秋光飛瀑.descriptionEn: Autumn light reaches a transformed realm; the flying falls enter the meditative heart.
秋光飛瀑.curatorNoteEn: A semi-abstract ink painting. Autumn reds twist and turn like verses of autumn poetry, a distant waterfall flies down, and mist drifts. Autumn red, waterfall, white water and faint light merge into one breath. Outwardly it is a flowing landscape — a wilderness, a snowy summit, or the world at its first beginning; inwardly it is a quiet, deep state of mind. Before the light fully dawns, life is already stirring: autumn water holding light, white mist and falling water — boundless scenery within a few square inches.

青松嵐影.descriptionEn: Houses tucked deep in the clouds, green pines trailing morning mist; mountain haze rises from far peaks, and the sight sets the mind adrift.
青松嵐影.curatorNoteEn: A tall hanging-scroll landscape in layered pale ink that conveys the flow of mist, light above and solid below, the energy connected throughout. Distant mountains hide in a sea of fog, there and not there; trees in the middle float and sink like smoke or a dream; in the foreground, gnarled pines in steady brushwork echo houses on the mountainside — a landscape to gaze at, wander through and live in. Cool but not cold, as if winter is ending and spring is near; light moves through the fog, and stillness holds movement.

翠嶺含煙.descriptionEn: From where does living rhythm come? Misty light sinks deep into the valley. Floating clouds know my mind; coming or going, as if without intent.
翠嶺含煙.curatorNoteEn: A landscape painted from life, with rich, moist ink as the base and fresh green color. Lush trees hold boundless life; steep cliffs rise in the middle ground and distant peaks appear through the haze. Clouds pass between the ridges and the forest rolls like waves — a rhythm of movement within stillness that places the viewer deep in the mountains, hearing wind in the pines, watching clouds leave the peaks, and feeling the endless life of heaven and earth.

清氣滿山.descriptionEn: Mountain haze floats on far peaks; clear air fills the empty mountains. Heaven and earth leave a scroll of poems; the universe comes and goes of itself.
清氣滿山.curatorNoteEn: A long-scroll landscape in pale ink, layers of mist covering mountains, forests and valleys, the brushwork barely there, seen and unseen. Empty white in the middle rises like a sea of clouds, the forest alternating dense and sparse, moist and serene. Houses appear faintly at lower right, a hint of human life that adds a sense of secluded dwelling. Close to the free brushwork of scholar painting, with something of the haziness of modern abstraction.

煙林水色.descriptionEn: Misty woods lightly brushed, water's colors without sound; heaven's workings flow and turn, and clarity comes of itself.
煙林水色.curatorNoteEn: Layers of wash between black and white, solid and empty, create an airy, silent waterside. Distant trees like smoke, the near shore moist, and where the water glimmers, a few white egrets break the silence — movement within stillness, spirit within lightness. It has the deep composition of classical landscape painting along with the texture and rhythm of modern abstraction.

山光含煙翠.titleEn: Mountain Light Veiled in Green Mist
山光含煙翠.descriptionEn: Mountain light holds green mist; the clear stream washes the dust from the heart.
山光含煙翠.curatorNoteEn: An elegant blue-green landscape. Nearby a small stream murmurs, with a little bridge and passers-by, calm and harmonious. A waterfall appears faintly in the distance; the trees are finely and rhythmically placed, and mist drifts through the forest.

白水丹楓-秋光.titleEn: White Water and Red Maples – Autumn Light
白水丹楓-秋光.descriptionEn: White water passes through the clouds; autumn light is bright to the eye. Holding mountains and valleys in the heart, motion and stillness come naturally.
白水丹楓-秋光.curatorNoteEn: A mountain forest dominated by sweeping red, like autumn maples or burning flames, interwoven with black and grey strokes as if moved by the wind. Distant mountains appear faintly through the mist, and a band of white left of center links down into a waterfall and stream. In the spirit of modern ink or Eastern abstract landscape, it emphasizes emotion and movement, expressing life at its most fully alive.

天光竹影-月世界.titleEn: Skylight and Bamboo Shadows – Moon World
天光竹影-月世界.descriptionEn: Strange peaks stack up in the Moon World; ink bamboo dances in the clear breeze. Ten thousand valleys reflect the skylight, all within the blink of an eye.
天光竹影-月世界.curatorNoteEn: The unusual terrain of the Moon World badlands and swaying ink bamboo express a lively bamboo grove and a dramatic landscape, layered with strong rhythm. Solid and empty interweave, wind seems to blow through the bamboo, and through the mist a ray of light touches the hilltop. Mountain and wind create a natural flowing energy, with a sense of the speed of time. A gleam of light breaks the dark, ten thousand bamboo stalks sway in the wind; mountain and wind dance together. Strength and softness, motion and stillness — the moment understood as eternity.

月世界金秋.titleEn: Golden Autumn in the Moon World
月世界金秋.descriptionEn: Clouds move over the Moon World's ridges; autumn dyes ten thousand bamboo stalks gold. Do not say the mountain looks desolate — life is hidden right here.
月世界金秋.curatorNoteEn: The rugged, moon-like badlands form the bones of this work, joined by the flowing movement of a golden bamboo forest and lightly drifting mist — strength and softness, motion and stillness in balance. Dry, textured strokes carve the mountain with vigor, layered like waves raised by the wind; warm color in the bamboo suggests late autumn. Great vitality in barren ground: an inspiring, modern image of life blooming brilliantly in adversity. Heaven and earth hold great beauty without speaking — the strength of stone, the softness of bamboo, all of nature's flow within one painting.

煙嵐深處.descriptionEn: Deep in the mountain mist, water murmurs.
煙嵐深處.curatorNoteEn: An elegant blue-green landscape: a murmuring stream nearby, houses hidden among the trees, and someone fishing on the bank, all wrapped in soft mist, calm and harmonious. Far peaks vanish into the clouds and a waterfall drops from a deep ravine. Mist, the sound of water, tree shadows and people blend into a quiet, fresh mountain world rich with the spirit of Zen.

禾木秋煙.descriptionEn: Autumn mist at Hemu is a poem in itself.
禾木秋煙.curatorNoteEn: An ink landscape painted from life at Hemu, often called China's most beautiful village, in autumn. Birch forests turn golden against clear, cloud-wrapped mountains, and small log cabins are scattered among them — peaceful, gentle, and far from the world's contentions.

武陵煙聲舞秋紅.titleEn: Wuling: Misty Falls amid Dancing Autumn Reds
武陵煙聲舞秋紅.descriptionEn: At Wuling, the Misty Sound Falls dance among the autumn reds.
武陵煙聲舞秋紅.curatorNoteEn: Autumn maples at Wuling Farm, with the distant Yansheng (Misty Sound) Falls woven into the scene. The flying waterfall and mountains of red maple set each other off, and the strong contrast of red and white shows the grandeur and liveliness of autumn mountains. The rushing falls fly like white silk while maple leaves color the slopes layer by layer — full of movement and the bright, warm feeling of autumn, nature's most moving season.

春滿人間.descriptionEn: Deep among the blossoms, even the clouds are white; on the warm grass the sheep begin to idle. Sitting long, spring says nothing; the wind blows and heaven and earth grow wide. A clear breeze greens the grass, flower shadows fill the spring hills; white sheep deep in the clouds, the wind blows and heaven and earth grow wide.
春滿人間.curatorNoteEn: A great grove of cherry blossoms above a green meadow, with a few goats scattered across it. In the distance the blossoms merge with drifting clouds — free, soft, open and warm, light and comfortable. The brushwork is varied and rhythmic, seemingly effortless yet precise in every stroke, sweeping out a beautiful scene of spring.
